linkedin_post.body:
Early mornings in a small kitchen. The smell of roasted coffee thick in the air. I was hand-labeling jars at 11 PM, exhausted, when a retailer friend stopped by. He picked up a prototype, turned it around, and frowned.

"Where's the chicory percentage?" he asked. "Every other brand hides it. If you're pure, prove it on the front."

That moment rewrote our packaging. Bold, Purista, and Purica now say pure coffee — zero chicory — right where the thumb rests. Purica is freeze-dried pure Arabica. Purista is freeze-dried pure Robusta. Bold is agglomerated pure coffee. Prima is pure Arabica agglomerated, currently unavailable. Ultra Blend wears its 70% coffee, 30% chicory badge proudly. No decoding. No flip-the-jar hunt.

The retailer came back two weeks later. "Now I don't have to explain it. The jar does my job."

Clean labels aren't a marketing tactic. They're respect for the person stocking the shelf and the person buying the jar.
